title: The draft: store, event log, routes, live stream
request: Home is where a problem becomes a solution: the user writes one sentence (or asks for any kind of model), brings data or not, and while the data is structured, cleaned and described in the background, a chat at the bottom asks a few questions about the real problem and an agent draws a solution workflow for this specific problem that follows the conversation. This package is the pre-project object everything on Home hangs on: the draft.
spec: dclab_rnd/draft/store.py (one folder per draft: draft.json, events.jsonl, data/), create/read/update/delete routes, and GET /api/drafts/{id}/events as a resumable server-sent event stream. Writes need the CSRF token; a missing or malformed body is a 422, never a 500. Done when the store tests and the upload-and-events-stream test pass.
plan: Write DraftStore under DCLAB_DRAFT_HOME with atomic saves, update(fn) under a per-draft lock, and an append-only event log with sequence numbers.
Hold in a draft: the problem, the pack, messages, questions, assets, the cleaning log, the analysis, the workflow, what the chat understood, and the status.
Add POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/drafts and the events route that replays from Last-Event-ID.
Mount the routes into the server, with draft jobs cancelled cleanly at shutdown.
Drive the Home flow end to end without a model and fix what the routes did wrong.

decisions.decision: A draft is its own object, separate from a project.
decisions.why: Home must hold a conversation, data being prepared and a workflow before anyone has decided what to build; a project only exists once the solution is accepted.

decisions.decision: Every change is also an event with a sequence number, and the stream replays from Last-Event-ID.
decisions.why: The page can reconnect after a network blip or a reload and catch up exactly, without missing a step of the pipeline or a chat message.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/store.py (DraftStore, atomic saves, locked update, event log) and dclab_rnd/draft/api.py (draft CRUD routes and the resumable event stream), mounted in the server.

findings.defect: Message ids built from the timestamp could collide.
findings.scenario: Two messages written in the same instant (for example the data-ready reply and a pipeline note) would get the same id, so the page would replace one with the other.
findings.cause: An id derived from time is unique only if writes never coincide.
findings.impact: When the data-ready reply and a pipeline note were written in the same instant, the page would key both by one id and show only one. The user would miss either the question about the outcome or the note about the data, with no error anywhere.

findings.defect: Draft routes answered 500 when a request body was missing or was not a JSON object.
findings.scenario: Running the Home flow end to end without a model, a PATCH with an empty body or a JSON list raised inside the route and the server answered 500.
findings.cause: The routes assumed a well-formed object.
findings.fix: Every draft route validates its body and answers 422 for a bad one; the proposal body became optional.
findings.test: Assertions for empty and wrong-shaped bodies added to tests/test_draft_flow.py.
findings.impact: A page or script that sent an empty or list-shaped body got a 500 and a stack trace in the server log instead of a 422 saying what was wrong. The caller could not tell its own mistake from a server fault, and the error would be counted against the server.

outcome: Done: drafts are stored with an event log and a resumable stream; bad bodies are 422.
lessons: A caller's mistake is a 4xx with a reason, never a 500; test the empty and the wrong-shaped body.
risks: The pipeline thread and a chat turn update one draft at the same time, and one update is lost without a per-draft lock.
A crash during a save leaves a half-written draft.json unless saves are atomic.
A page that reconnects after a network blip misses pipeline steps or chat messages unless the stream replays from Last-Event-ID.
Malformed request bodies reach route code and come back as 500s instead of 422s.
Draft jobs still running at shutdown keep writing to a store that is closing.
